best-octopus-go-alternative.html.pre: * All rates pulled 21 October 2026. Octopus Go: GO-FIX-12M-26-10-14, issued on 20 October. EDF: EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_12M_V3_HH (Go Electric 12m v3) and EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_18M_V4_HH (Go Electric 18m v4). EDF launched the 18m v4 on 21 October with the same standing charges as v3 and a peak rate about 1p/kWh higher in every region; the 12m v3, on sale since 18 September, is unchanged, and the 18m v3 was still listed as available on the day v4 appeared. The two EDF tariffs do not share a standing charge. The 18-month is about 2.2p/kWh cheaper at peak and about 5.5p a day cheaper on standing charge than the 12-month, so on today's prices it is the cheaper EDF tariff on every line except the exit fee (£100 rather than £75) and the six-month longer tie-in. Both keep the 6.99p/kWh off-peak rate. Against Octopus Go, the 18-month has the lower peak rate in every region and is within about 2p a day on standing charge either way. The 12-month now has the lower peak rate in every region, London included, but its standing charge is 3 to 7.5p a day higher than Octopus Go’s. Octopus reissued Go on 20 October: the off-peak rate came down from 9.50p to 9.87p, the peak rate rose by between 0.7p and 2.8p/kWh depending on region, and standing charges moved by up to 2.7p a day either way. All figures include VAT at 5%. Note that VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain drops from 5% to 0% between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2027, which will cut every rate here by about 4.8% — suppliers' own quotes may already be shown at 0%. Rates are baked into this page at time of writing — always verify on each supplier's website before switching.
